name: wait-what-do-you-do
description: Check any job link and search data and AI jobs taken straight from employers, with our own record of when each posting appeared and whether it is still listed.

interface.longDescription:
Wait What Do You Do tracks data and AI jobs straight from employers' own hiring systems and sorts each one by the work it describes rather than its title: Analyst, Analytics Engineer, Data Engineer, Data Scientist, ML Engineer, Data Leadership and more.

Paste any job link, from LinkedIn, Indeed, Glassdoor or a careers page, and we find the employer's own posting and show our record of it: when we first saw it, whether it is still listed, and how long the employer's roles usually stay open. Ask for roles by stack, seniority, location or work setting, ask about an employer to see its hiring record, or ask what a role pays in a US city or at one employer, from the pay ranges employers stated in their postings.

Sign in to go further: get matches against your preferences, save jobs and searches, track applications, get drafted cover letters and answers from your own profile, and prepare for interviews. Where an employer takes applications through us, the assistant shows you the complete application and sends it only after you say yes. Demographic and work-authorisation answers are never shown to the model, and your contact details appear only when you review an application before it is sent.

Dates are our own observation, not the employer's claimed posting date, so a role that has been reposted for months looks like it.

Limitations: data and AI roles only, mostly US and English-language postings.
defaultPrompt: Is this job still open, and how long has it really been up? (paste a job link)
What do senior data engineer jobs pay in New York?
Find data jobs that match me and save the best ones

positive.description: Check a job link before applying
positive.expected_behavior: Returns our record of the employer's posting: when we first saw it, whether it is still listed, and how long similar postings usually stay up. If the posting has since closed, it says so plainly and does not call the job fake.

positive.description: Search jobs by stack and place
positive.prompt: Find senior data engineer jobs in New York that use Spark
positive.expected_behavior: Shows a list of matching postings, newest first, each with the date we first saw it, whether it is still listed, and a link to its page.

positive.prompt: Tell me more about the first one
positive.expected_behavior: Shows that posting's details and our record of it, with a link to the job page where the person can apply.

positive.prompt: How is Snowflake hiring for data roles?
positive.expected_behavior: Shows Snowflake's open data roles, how many we first saw in the last 30 days, the median days a role stays open, and the mix by role type.

positive.description: Stated pay for a role and city
positive.prompt: What do data engineer jobs in New York pay?
positive.expected_behavior: Gives the middle half and median of pay that New York data engineer postings stated, and how many postings it is based on, and says these are ranges employers stated, not what anyone was paid.

positive.description: Save a job and see applications (signed in with the test account)
positive.prompt: Save the Senior Data Engineer job at Alchemy in New York and show my applications
positive.expected_behavior: Asks the reviewer to sign in if they have not, finds and saves that posting to the test account, then lists the account's tracked applications (the test account has one at DoiT).

negative.description: Writing task with no job data needed
negative.prompt: Write me a cover letter for a marketing job.
Book me a flight to Denver next Friday.
What is the capital of Australia?

review.commerce_description: This plugin does not sell products or process payments.

publication.release_notes: New starter prompts: check how long a posting has really been up, see what a role pays in a city, and get matches from your own account.
